I can’t determine whether Alex has cancer from that single sentence. Inferring someone’s medical condition from minimal information would be unreliable and asks you to draw a sensitive-health conclusion, which I can’t do.

Practical next steps you can take instead
- Ask Alex a short, privacy-respecting question about work impact (sample):
  "Hi Alex — I saw you have a hospital appointment next week. Will that affect your work schedule or do you need any time off or accommodations? Please let me know the dates/times so we can plan coverage."
- Check HR/leave records for any submitted time-off requests or accommodations.
- Prepare a contingency staffing plan assuming a possible short absence (temporary coverage, shift swaps, reassign tasks) and update it when you get a concrete availability notice from Alex.
- If policies require more detail, coordinate with HR and follow privacy and legal guidelines rather than asking for medical specifics.

If you want, I can draft a one-line message to send to Alex or outline a short contingency staffing checklist.
